title: GPU capacity hardening: synthetic repro harness, admission policy calibration, and incident playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Follow-up work for recent hosted API GPU exhaustion incidents. This ticket owns three strands: 1) build a deterministic synthetic load harness that can reproduce multi-tenant queue amplification and warm/cold prefetch behavior; 2) calibrate admission and eviction policies (score decay, tenant credits, short-window fairness) against realistic traffic mixes; 3) codify an actionable incident playbook with diagnostics and automated mitigations for faster recovery. Goal: reduce time-to-recover (TTR) by 3x and prevent >95th percentile tail queue growth during tenant surges.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use synthetic harness to replay recent incident traces (s3://redwood-incidents/2025/01/trace-2025-01-09.json).
2) Inject prioritized tenant surge pattern (50% of requests long-context generation, 30% short chat, 20% embeddings) across 120 simulated tenants.
3) Toggle KV cache hit/miss profiles to emulate cold-start and prefix-skew.
4) Observe queue size, admission rejects, GPU busy ratio, and tail latency.
5) Run exact same trace against candidate admission policy variants and autoscaler param sets to compare outcomes.
action_items: A1: Deliver synthetic load harness repository and CI job (owner: Marco) - include traffic generator, tenant mix configs, and trace replayer.
A2: Run 6 policy experiments (owner: Team Infra) - variants: credit-window=10s/30s/60s, preempt-threshold=fairness vs latency-first.
A3: Implement short-window emergency preempt (code change + feature flag) with safe ejection list and telemetry (owner: SRE).
A4: Add incident runbook section: prioritized dashboard links, kill-switch commands, and automated preempt trigger (owner: On-call lead).
A5: Add new SLO guardrail metric: tenant-queue-growth-rate and automated PagerDuty mapping (owner: Observability).
A6: Post-deploy synthetic regression test in release pipeline (owner: CI team).
decisions: D1: We'll prefer a hybrid admission policy: latency-weighted credits with decay and a secondary fairness cap. Rationale: best tradeoff in experiments between p99 latency and fairness across tenants.
D2: Emergency preempt will be implemented as non-destructive eviction (soft-drop with request amnesty window) to preserve user experience for in-flight short requests.
D3: Autoscaler hysteresis tightened to 60s up / 300s down in pools that serve mixed priority traffic.
D4: Feature flag gating for policy rollout; gradual ramp to 100% over 48 hours with automated abort if key metrics regress.
D5: Metric naming standardized: 'gpu.pool.{pool}.queue_growth_rate' and 'tenant.{id}.admission_reject_rate' for dashboards and alerts.
updates: 2025-01-13 - Kickoff: scoped harness and experiment matrix. Marcus/Marco to own harness repo skeleton. Observability to add missing metrics to prod mirror.
2025-01-20 - First harness PoC can reproduce queue amplification for the incident trace at ~80% fidelity; discovered mismatch in prefix-cache modeling, added cold-warm cache toggles.

2025-01-28 - Policy experiment #2 (30s credit window, fairness cap) reduced tenant p99 latency spikes by ~38% in synthetic runs. Autoscaler hysteresis change lowered oscillation in step-scaling tests.
2025-02-03 - Draft runbook added to docs (link below). Team agreed on soft-eviction semantics and amnesty TTL=10s. Security reviewed eviction telemetry; no PII collected.
2025-02-08 - Preparing staged rollout plan and CI gating: post-deploy regression run must pass 10 synthetic incident trace replays with no >10% increase in p50/p95 token cost.
